answer: Cross-epoch behavioural thread matching. Each identity carries a thread of logged actions; at epoch boundaries the agent must show that its new behaviour is consistent with that history within a similarity threshold. New or merged identities sit on a hollow track with few prior actions, so they fail the match and are capped in influence until real history accumulates. To pass, an attacker must run each fake identity across many epochs, sustaining realistic behaviour near a ledge of the threshold, paying continuous compute and attention per identity instead of a one-time fee.
